projects.title: SEER
projects.description: SEER is a smart fishing assistant designed to help fishermen find better fishing spots instead of wasting hours searching manually. It uses a floating sensor device placed in the sea to collect real-time environmental data such as water temperature, water quality, turbidity, pH, TDS, wave and wind conditions, water pressure, and GPS location. SEER then analyzes this data and compares it with information about fish habitat preferences to identify areas where specific fish are more likely to be found. The system displays this information on a map, showing fishermen recommended fishing locations and the types of fish they are likely to catch. This allows fishermen to make decisions based on actual environmental data rather than relying only on experience or trial and error, helping them reduce search time, fuel consumption, and unsuccessful fishing trips.

projects.title: GHARSA
projects.description: GHARSA is an e-commerce platform designed to connect customers with plant sellers and greenhouses in Jordan, making it easier to discover, compare, and purchase plants online. The platform focuses on providing information about different plants, including their suitable temperature and humidity ranges, care requirements, categories, and prices in Jordanian dinars. GHARSA aims to simplify the process of buying plants by bringing multiple plant options into one online marketplace, helping customers find plants that match their environment and needs while giving greenhouses and plant sellers a digital platform to showcase and sell their products.

projects.title: Operating System Development Aenix-Os
projects.description: Aenix-OS is a custom operating system project developed from scratch to explore the fundamental concepts of operating systems and low-level computer architecture. It involves building the core software responsible for booting the computer, managing hardware and memory, handling CPU operations, and providing the basic environment required for programs to run.

projects.title: Linux From Scratch
projects.description: Linux From Scratch (LFS) is a project that teaches how to build a complete Linux-based operating system from the ground up. Instead of installing a prebuilt distribution, you manually compile and configure the system’s essential components, including the compiler, libraries, core utilities, and Linux kernel. This provides a deeper understanding of how Linux works internally, how its components interact, and how an operating system is assembled and configured.

projects.title: Mentora
projects.description: Mentora is a mentoring platform designed to connect students and learners with mentors who can guide them in developing their technical, academic, and career skills. The platform provides a structured environment where users can find suitable mentors, communicate with them, receive guidance, set goals, and track their progress, making the mentoring process more organized and accessible.

achievements.title: 3rd Place — HTU Blue Horizons Hackathon
achievements.description: SEER, a marine fishing support system combining environmental sensor data, GPS, and software analytics to help fishermen identify potential fishing areas and reduce wasted time and resources. The project qualified for the Blue Horizons Exhibition in Aqaba.

about.title:

about.intro:
Computer Science student and software developer based in Amman, Jordan. I like understanding how things work, then making them useful — from the operating system up to the interface someone touches.

This machine is a small tour through the work, tools, and questions I keep returning to. It is intentionally old-fashioned. The engineering is not.

sections.title: In Depth
sections.description:
About Me

I am Ahmad Omar Abu Elsamen, a fourth-year Computer Science student at Al Hussein Technical University (HTU), based in Amman, Jordan. I am passionate about software development, computer systems, and building practical solutions that solve real problems. Throughout my university journey, I have focused not only on learning programming concepts but also on applying them through projects, competitions, hackathons, and hands-on technical work. I enjoy understanding how things work at a deeper level, from software and databases to operating systems, networks, and hardware.

My technical background covers several areas of computer science. I have experience with C, Java, JavaScript, Python, MATLAB, SQL, and Assembly, along with web technologies such as HTML, CSS, React, and Node.js. I have worked with relational databases and SQL, and I am comfortable working in Linux environments and using Bash. I also have experience with networking and cybersecurity concepts, including TCP/IP and Wireshark. In embedded systems, I have worked with Arduino and ESP32 boards, sensors, communication modules, and hardware-software integration. I am particularly interested in understanding systems from the lower level and have explored areas such as operating systems, Linux, and Linux From Scratch.

I also enjoy competitive programming because it has strengthened the way I approach problems. I have solved more than 150 problems on Codeforces, which has helped me improve my algorithmic thinking, problem-solving skills, and ability to work under time constraints. Competitive programming taught me to break complicated problems into smaller parts, identify patterns, and develop efficient solutions rather than simply looking for something that works.

A major part of my university experience has been turning ideas into complete projects. One of my most important projects is SEER, a smart fishing solution that I developed around the idea of helping fishermen make better decisions about where to fish. SEER uses environmental and location data such as temperature, water conditions, pressure, waves, wind, and GPS information to help identify areas that may be suitable for specific fish. The project combines embedded hardware, sensors, data processing, databases, and a user interface into one system. SEER was developed as part of the Blue Horizons Hackathon at HTU, where it achieved third place and qualified for exhibition in Aqaba.

Another project I have worked on is GHARSA, an e-commerce platform focused on selling plants in Jordan. The project combines e-commerce with useful information about plants, including environmental requirements such as temperature and humidity. I worked on the website, product and category structure, design, custom code, pricing in Jordanian dinars, payment methods, and additional features such as a chatbot. GHARSA was also entered into an e-commerce website competition, where the project achieved second place. This project gave me experience beyond programming because I had to think about the customer, the market, the business model, the user experience, and how a technical product could actually operate as a business.

I have also participated in technical and academic activities that helped me develop both my technical and teamwork skills. I worked as a Junior Database Developer for an HTU team in the Crown Prince Competition for Best Government Application in 2024. I also participated in the Jordan Young Scientists Exhibition through JOYS and have worked on projects involving databases, cybersecurity, embedded systems, web development, and software engineering. These experiences taught me how to work with others, communicate technical ideas, manage project requirements, and turn an initial idea into something that can actually be demonstrated and evaluated.

Beyond individual technologies, I am interested in understanding the complete process of building technology. I enjoy moving from identifying a problem, to designing a solution, choosing the appropriate technologies, developing the system, testing it, and finally thinking about how people would actually use it. This is one reason I have become increasingly interested in the connection between technology and business. I do not want to focus only on writing code; I want to understand why a product should exist, who needs it, how it creates value, and how it can become a sustainable business.

My long-term goal is to become a strong software and systems professional while developing the business skills needed to build my own companies and startups. I want to gain experience in both technical and business environments, particularly in situations where I can interact with people, understand real problems, and turn those problems into practical solutions. I believe that being able to understand both the technology and the business behind a product will allow me to build better solutions and eventually create products of my own.

At this stage of my career, I am focused on continuing to improve as a developer, gaining real-world experience, working on challenging projects, and learning from people with different technical and business backgrounds. I am especially interested in opportunities involving software development, systems, backend development, databases, embedded systems, and problem-solving. I see every project and experience as an opportunity to learn something new, improve the way I work, and move closer to my goal of becoming someone who can take an idea from a problem all the way to a working product.
